To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

induced innovation is the dominant source of technical change in agriculture, evolutionary theory is the dominant source in industry, and path dependence is the dominant source for the evolution of the institutional framework for technical change.

induced innovation, evolutionary theory and path dependence are all sources of technical change, but that each of these sources is more important in some contexts and at some times than in others, and that the three are complementary rather than mutually exclusive.

the induced innovation hypothesis is a useful tool for understanding the effects of changes in relative prices on the rate of technical change.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the sources of technical changes are not limited to changes in demand and factor prices, but also include changes in the institutional environment and the social structure of technical change.
the sources of technical changes are not confined to the research laboratories of universities and private firms, but are also embedded in the institutions of civil society.
technical change is a process that is shaped by the interaction of the three sources of change: induced innovation, evolutionary change, and historical path dependency.
